text: {"lessons":["Selling Stock A, C, and D at gains and later buying some back at lower prices did not prove that the timing was wise; I should evaluate decisions against a consistent plan, not the comfort of realized gains.","After buying A, C, and D again, I should reassess each holding using its current risk and expected return rather than anchoring on either my average cost or its recent price path.","My account value fluctuated while I made no trades, reinforcing that short-term changes are not reliable signals; I should review diversification and cash deliberately instead of reacting to noise."]}
